summary: Belah was a 120-foot La Salle Parish fire tower, set to stop being manned in July 1985 and now listed as torn down.

facts.status_note: Wikipedia lists the tower as torn down; no removal date is given.

events.note: Rainfall of 47.39 inches recorded at the tower in 1956, reported in January 1957
Rain gauge at the tower measured about six inches in a July 1969 storm, reprinted in a 2009 column
Planned end of manned watch after July 1, 1985, per a March 1985 report

evidence.supports: Belah is listed among Louisiana's fire lookout towers
state had 39 fire towers by 1943 and 56 by 1950
evidence.quote: By 1943 thirty-nine fire towers had been built and by 1950 the number had increased to fifty-six.

evidence.supports: list marks the tower as torn down
site could not be viewed on street view or older aerial imagery
evidence.quote: Unable to view on street view or older aerial imagery.

evidence.supports: tower height 120 feet in March 1985 report
evidence.quote: Belah is 120 feet tall and a steep climb.

evidence.supports: State Forester said tower would no longer be manned after July 1
evidence.quote: Belah Fire Tower will be one of many firetowers in north Louisiana which will no longer be manned after July 1

evidence.supports: some crews expected to keep watching for fires from the towers
evidence.quote: But some crews say they expect to be watching for fires from the towers even after the change.
Total rainfall recorded at the Belah fire tower in LaSalle parish in 1956 was 47.39 inches

evidence.supports: rain gauge at the tower measured about six inches in a July 1969 storm
evidence.quote: The rain gauge at the Belah Fire Tower measured about six inches in about that many hours.

sources.title: List of fire lookout towers in Louisiana
Belah - Forest Lookouts
sources.publisher: Louisiana Lookouts (centraluslookouts.weebly.com), quoting The Town Talk, The Monroe News-Star and the Jena Times

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The March 1985 report gives a planned end to manned watches after July 1, 1985, and says some crews expected to keep watching. The record treats that as a plan, not a confirmed end date.

notes_for_editor: No build date and no fire history found in two searches and the reads. The Wikipedia row and the Forest Lookouts page are the only Belah-specific sources. The Former Fire Lookout Sites Louisiana list (six sites) does not include Belah, Bodcau or Clinton. No source describes the site today.
